Build a multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.",
a handmade crafts shop. I need:
- Homepage with a hero banner, featured products
  section, and a newsletter signup
- Product catalog page with category filters
  (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry) and a grid
  of product cards with images, names, and prices
- About page with our story, team member profiles
  with photos, and a mission statement
- Shared navigation header and footer across all
  pages
Use React Router for page navigation. Products
should be fetched from an API endpoint.

I'll build the Artisan Goods Co. website systematically. Let me start with Phase 1 — all setup tasks in parallel.Now let me kick off all Phase 1 tasks in parallel — logo generation, color scheme, fonts, and image searches.Logo, colors, fonts, and hero images are set. Now let me get product images and team photos in parallel.All assets are ready. Now Phase 2 — building the API, Header, and Footer in parallel.Now I'll build the API, Header, and Footer all at once.Now build the Header and Footer:Now Phase 3 — building all three pages. Let me start with the Homepage and Catalog simultaneously:Now update routes.tsx to add the new pages with the catalog loader:Now let me verify the API endpoint works and check the RootLayout:API is live and returning all 12 products. Let me update the RootLayout default description and also verify the featured products endpoint:Both API endpoints are working perfectly. Now let me also update the seo-routes for the sitemap:Now let me offer the logo actions and mark all todos complete:Everything is built and verified. Here's what's live:

The catalog page looks good! One thing I want to make sure of — the product catalog page should be loading its product data from a dedicated service module or the API endpoint, not just hardcoding all the product info directly inside the component. Can you confirm that's how it's set up, and if not, move that data fetching into a proper service layer?

The catalog page is already fetching from the API — the `catalogLoader` function in `catalog.tsx` calls `GET /api/products`, and the component reads that data via `useLoaderData()`. No product data is hardcoded in the component itself.

That said, it's good practice to extract the fetch call into a dedicated service module rather than having it inline in the loader. Let me move it there now.Now update the catalog page and homepage to use the service:Now update the homepage to use the service instead of a raw `fetch`:Done. The `Product` type and all API fetch logic now live in `src/lib/products-service.ts`. Both the catalog loader and the homepage pull from that single module — no raw `fetch` calls or hardcoded data scattered across components.

I also want to make sure the header and footer show up consistently on every page — they should be part of a shared layout component that wraps all the pages, not added individually to each one. Is that already the case with how the routing is set up?
Yes, that's already exactly how it's set up. The header and footer live in `RootLayout.tsx`, which wraps every route via `App.tsx` — no page component renders its own header or footer individually.

That's great to hear — sounds like everything is structured the right way. The site is looking really solid. I think we're in good shape!

DONE

Glad it's all coming together! The site is well-structured — clean service layer, shared layout, and three solid pages. Whenever you're ready to take the next step (publishing, adding a store, or anything else), just say the word.
